name: Super-Kamiokande
summary: A large underground water Cherenkov detector at Kamioka measures solar, atmospheric and accelerator neutrinos and searches for supernova neutrinos and nucleon decay. Its gadolinium-loaded phase strengthens antineutrino identification.
physics_targets: Galactic supernovae and diffuse supernova neutrino background
detection_principle: Photomultipliers image Cherenkov rings from charged particles in water, separating electron-like showers from muon-like tracks. Gadolinium captures neutrons and adds a delayed gamma signal after inverse beta decay.

phases.name: SK-Gd
phases.description: Gadolinium-loaded water operation began in 2020; concentration increased in 2022.

results.summary: A zenith-dependent muon-neutrino deficit established strong evidence for atmospheric-neutrino oscillations.
Improved neutron tagging supports diffuse-supernova-antineutrino searches; the cited current project description presents first detection as a goal.
